title: Sharp selfishness threshold for manipulation-resistant tournaments
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: For every n≥1, is there a monotone Condorcet-consistent randomized tournament rule satisfying 2-NM₁?
definitions: A tournament T on labeled teams [n] orients exactly one edge between each distinct pair, with i→j meaning i defeats j. A rule r assigns a probability vector (r_1(T),…,r_n(T)) of nonnegative reals summing to one. Condorcet consistency requires r_i(T)=1 if i defeats every other team. Monotonicity requires r_i(T)≥r_i(T′) whenever T′ is obtained by changing only the outcome i→j to j→i. For every two tournaments T,T′ differing only on the match between distinct i,j, require the exact inequality r_i(T′)+r_j(T′)≤r_i(T)+r_j(T)+max{r_i(T)−r_i(T′), r_j(T)−r_j(T′)}. Both ordered directions (T,T′) must satisfy it. This is the source’s selfishness-parameter-one condition; no additive error is allowed. The quantifiers are ∀n ∃r_n ∀T,T′,i,j. No efficiency, anonymity or consistency between different n is imposed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the proposition or its negation for the stated model. A construction at any larger fixed selfishness parameter, or only for finitely many team counts, does not establish the proposition.
context: The 2025 paper gives a constant selfishness parameter and records the barrier below one, leaving the sharp endpoint distinct from existence of some constant.
why: A sharp incentive threshold would identify how much internal sacrifice is needed to prevent collusion in tournament selection.

import_provenance.original_title: The sharp selfishness threshold for manipulation-resistant tournaments
import_provenance.original_statement: Does every number of teams admit a monotone, Condorcet-consistent randomized tournament rule satisfying 2-NM₁? Under this condition a pair cannot gain more total winning probability by fixing its match than the probability sacrificed by the team that loses deliberately.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The December 2025 construction already achieves the constant threshold 11; the open conjecture is the optimal threshold 1, not merely the existence of any constant.

sentences: The input gives the winner of every pairwise match.
A tournament rule selects an overall winner by a probability distribution.
A team winning all its matches must be selected with certainty.
Changing a win to a loss must not improve that team’s own chance.
The exact pairwise inequality fixes the remaining selfishness threshold at one.
